raw.title: Focus ring
raw.description: Customize visible keyboard focus with inherited root and contextual theme tokens.
raw.lead: Customize visible keyboard focus with inherited root and contextual theme tokens.

sections.heading: Example
sections.example: Review button styles

code.source: Review button styles

paragraphs: Use focus-ring on a native link or button. It styles focus-visible but does not make a generic element interactive. Reach this example with the keyboard to see its outline.

sections.heading: Variants and custom colors
sections.example: Contextual focus ring
paragraphs: The outline uses --trm-focus-ring-width and chooses --trm-theme-focus-ring before --trm-focus-ring-color. A theme modifier therefore takes priority over a custom default focus color. There is no legacy focus-color fallback or generated focus-ring-primary class.

Root defaults are a 3px width, a 1px offset token and a color referencing --trm-primary-focus-ring. The helper class does not itself apply outline-offset; add that declaration explicitly when desired. The focus mixin can apply it through its first argument.

sections.heading: Root token configuration
paragraphs: Preload the root token map before the full entry. Geometry is not configured through standalone focus-ring-width or focus-ring-offset Sass options on the main entry. Local CSS custom properties can override the root values without recompiling.

sections.heading: Sass
paragraphs: Import the mixin from its owning module. focus-ring($offset: false, $color: null) uses the runtime width token when an explicit color is supplied; otherwise it uses --trm-focus-ring. The first argument opts into the offset token. Load framework root styles separately when consuming these tokens.

sections.heading: Verification
paragraphs: Check keyboard focus, zoom, adjacent surfaces, clipping and forced colors. The pinned helper does not add a forced-colors Highlight override; native browser behavior still needs testing. Do not remove an outline without providing an equally usable focus indicator.

raw.title: Hover lift
raw.description: Give interactive elements a small elevation cue on hover and visible keyboard focus.
raw.lead: Give interactive elements a small elevation cue on hover and visible keyboard focus.

sections.heading: How it works
paragraphs: The pinned helper applies translateY(-.25rem) and a shadow on hover and focus-visible. It owns four tokens: transition duration (.2s), timing (ease), transform and shadow. Its default shadow references --trm-box-shadow-lg. Use a native link or button; the class supplies no activation behavior.

sections.heading: Example
sections.example: Read the Card guide

code.source: Read the Card guide

paragraphs: Hover or keyboard-focus the link. Its destination and focus boundary remain understandable without movement. The helper is included in the full and utilities-only entries.

sections.heading: CSS
paragraphs: Set tokens on the element or in an application rule after the framework. Helper-owned declarations supersede values inherited from a parent. The shared transition, reduced-motion and shadow Sass switches control generated effects; disabling transitions or shadows does not remove the transform.

sections.heading: Sass token map
paragraphs: Configure the owning helper before loading the full entry. Map values merge with defaults; null removes a token declaration, not the declaration consuming that token. Configure the shared config module first if you also change its options.

sections.heading: Reduced motion
paragraphs: With a reduced-motion preference, the helper keeps its raised state but omits its transition. An application that wants no translation can override the transform token in that media query. Setting enable-reduced-motion to false explicitly opts out of the conditional transition.

raw.title: Position
raw.description: Place fixed and viewport-responsive sticky elements without obscuring content.
raw.lead: Place fixed and viewport-responsive sticky elements without obscuring content.

sections.heading: Fixed top and bottom

code.source:
<!-- Reserve layout space when using fixed bars. -->
<header class="fixed-top">Persistent header</header>
<footer class="fixed-bottom">Persistent actions</footer>

paragraphs: Fixed helpers use physical inset shorthands and --trm-z-fixed. They leave normal flow, so reserve enough application space and test text zoom, safe areas and the on-screen keyboard. These are code-only examples to avoid covering the documentation.

sections.heading: Sticky top
sections.example:
Sticky heading

Scroll within this region. The heading stays inside its containing scroll area.

Sticky placement remains in normal flow.

Check ancestor overflow and available scrolling space.

code.source:
Sticky heading

Scroll within this region. The heading stays inside its containing scroll area.

Sticky placement remains in normal flow.

Check ancestor overflow and available scrolling space.

paragraphs: sticky-top sets position: sticky, top: 0 and z-index: var(--trm-z-sticky). sticky-bottom uses bottom: 0. The helper has no literal z-index fallback; include root tokens or supply that token yourself.

sections.heading: Responsive positioning

code.source:
Always sticky at the physical bottom edge
Sticky from the md viewport breakpoint
Sticky from lg

paragraphs: Canonical prefixes use viewport range queries: md starts at 768px. They are not stack-container queries, and no infix or xxl aliases are generated. Below the threshold, an element retains ordinary positioning unless another rule changes it.

Both base and responsive position declarations have normal priority in the helpers layer. They do not include important declarations or a second utility-layer copy. Avoid contradictory position classes; generated CSS order, not HTML class order, controls conflicts.

sections.heading: Physical edges and configuration
paragraphs: Top and bottom remain physical edges in vertical writing modes, matching the pin. Fixed insets also remain physical. Configure the shared breakpoint map before the helper; the same map supplies responsive stack container thresholds. There is no separate legacy CQ scale.

Scope --trm-z-sticky or --trm-z-fixed to customize layer values. Ordinary z-index still cannot cross an ancestor stacking context or outrank the native top layer. Keep focused controls and anchored headings clear of persistent bars.

raw.title: Stacks
raw.description: Compose horizontal and vertical groups with container-responsive stack controls.
raw.lead: Compose horizontal and vertical groups with container-responsive stack controls.

sections.heading: Vertical
sections.example:
First item
Second item
Third item

code.source:
First item
Second item
Third item

paragraphs: vstack selects column direction and stretched items. It supplies no gap; add a spacing utility such as gap-3. Stack classes affect visual composition, not list or group semantics.

sections.heading: Horizontal
sections.example: Actions wrap when necessary.

code.source: Actions wrap when necessary.

paragraphs: hstack selects row direction with flex-start alignment. Add flex-wrap when wrapping is wanted. Both stacks use flex: 1 1 auto and align-self: stretch unless their input tokens change. There are no legacy stack or cluster classes in the strict core. The controls shown here use the inverse theme for readable labels. The pinned primary solid variant has only about 3.56:1 white-on-blue contrast at normal 16px text in light mode; variant names are not an accessibility guarantee. Check actual foreground and background pairs.

sections.heading: Container-responsive stacks
sections.example: First regionSecond region

code.source: First regionSecond region

paragraphs: stack-container establishes inline-size containment. Put the responsive stack inside it: a container cannot query itself. vstack sm:hstack switches to a row at the nearest eligible container minimum of 576px, independent of viewport width. md uses 768px.

The pinned base selectors match any class attribute containing hstack or vstack. Prefix-only names therefore establish a flex box before their query matches, normally with inherited direction or the row fallback. Application class names containing those substrings can also match. These inheriting controls can affect nested stacks; set a local base class when independence is needed.

sections.heading: Viewport-responsive alternative

code.source:
First region
Second region

paragraphs: Use responsive flex utilities when the viewport, rather than a query container, should control direction. Keep DOM and keyboard order meaningful. Do not reverse reading order merely to rearrange the visual layout.

sections.heading: CSS
paragraphs: Stack inputs are --trm-stack-flex, --trm-stack-direction, --trm-stack-align-items and --trm-stack-align-self. They are inheriting helper controls, not registered utility composition properties. Use normal gap utilities for spacing. The full and utilities-only entries include these helpers.

Container queries use physical width at this pin. Test unusual writing modes, nesting, intrinsic sizing, long labels, RTL and zoom. Give contained layouts an appropriate available size instead of assuming shrink-to-fit behavior is unchanged.

sections.heading: Container Sass helpers
paragraphs: Import query mixins from layout/breakpoints. set-container accepts a containment type and optional name. The up/down/only mixins accept a breakpoint, optional container name and optional map; between accepts the two bounds first.

The smallest zero minimum emits content without a query. Unknown keys also yield unqueried content at this pin, so keep map names coherent rather than relying on validation that the source does not provide.

sections.heading: Sass
paragraphs: Configure before or after on the owning module before loading the full entry. The pin forwards the configured pseudo-element name without a Sass validation error for other names; only choose a real pseudo-element appropriate to the browser behavior.

raw.title: Vertical rule
raw.description: Separate adjacent regions with a decorative physical vertical rule.
raw.lead: Separate adjacent regions with a decorative physical vertical rule.

sections.heading: How it works

Changing color alone does not recolor the rule. Set its boundary token instead. Physical width and minimum height do not swap axes with vertical writing modes.
